answer: When k bonded identities equivocate in a correlated pattern, the protocol links their signed evidence and applies a quadratic penalty, scaling as O(k²), rather than treating each key as an isolated offender. Escrowed collateral makes the cost enforceable; asymmetric depreciation compounds the loss, so a detected sybil swarm faces an exponential multiplier in capital loss. Like a ripple crossing a terrace, one provable act can expose many linked keys; opal-like polish offers no protection.
